summary.headline: Ambuja Cements guided FY27 volumes to ~80 Mt (~8% growth) and cut capex to INR6,000-6,500 crore, with cost peaking at INR4,500/t and a INR250/t reduction targeted.
summary.overview: Ambuja (consolidated, including ACC and Orient references) reported FY26 record volumes of 73.7 Mt (+16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (+31%, INR887/t, +12%), with PAT of INR2,647 crore (+17%). Q4 was weak operationally: volumes were muted, cost per tonne rose to about INR4,500 in the quarter against an earlier INR4,000 exit aspiration, and acquired assets (Sanghi at 57%, Penna at 46% utilization) lagged. Management reset its growth timeline, pushed capex out, and set a INR250/t cost reduction target for FY27. Pricing was flat-to-slightly-up at about INR254/bag, with industry realisations pressured by soft demand.

financial_highlights.change: March month about INR4,100/t before ~INR250 war-related escalation
about INR1 QoQ, flat YoY vs INR255

segments.name: Cement volumes
segments.commentary: FY26 volumes 73.7 Mt, trade sales volume grew about 10%; Q4 volume growth was muted, with Orient-adjusted volumes described as roughly flat YoY by one analyst.

segments.name: Acquired assets (Sanghi, Penna, Orient)
segments.commentary: Sanghi cement utilization about 57% and Penna about 46%; Orient running at full capacity. Management targets 5-10% utilization uplift at Penna and Sanghi (19 Mt combined capacity).

segments.name: Premium cement
segments.commentary: Premium cement was 35% of trade sales for FY26 and about 36% in Q4; management views 36% as sustainable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume target about 80 Mt, roughly 8% growth, against industry growth of about 5-5.5%.
FY27 cost reduction of about INR250/t on a full-year average basis, implying about INR4,250/t; management calls INR4,500/t the peak and expects Q1 FY27 roughly flat.
Additional cost savings of INR150-200/t cited from fly ash and green energy; minimum INR250/t reduction again targeted in FY28.
Capacity to reach about 119 Mt by end FY27 from about 109 Mt, with about 10 Mt of additions to be commissioned between now and September; FY28 capacity target may slip to around FY30.
FY27 capex guided at INR6,000-6,500 crore; roughly INR4 billion (about INR400 crore) already under execution.
Project IRR hurdle of 18% stated for new capex; 15 Mt debottlenecking retained but timing to vary.
capex_capacity: Capacity 109 Mt at FY26 end; clinker capacity 69 Mt, with 4 Mt clinker at Maratha to add next.
Commissioned 10.7 Mt grinding capacity in FY26 (Marwar, Farakka, Sankrail, Sindri, Krishnapatnam) plus 7 Mt clinker at Jodhpur and Bhatapara.
Proposed new clinker lines: Mundra (about 2 Mt) and Assam limestone block (about 2 Mt), targeted in about 24-28 months; Dahej Line 2 cited as a coastal example.
Recalibration: shifting to grinding units closer to markets (North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat, Maharashtra); Sanghi moving toward clinker over three years.
Seven vessels ordered for Sanghi marine logistics, deliveries from next year; Naliya rail line treated as an add-on, not in base case.
Efficiency capex delayed by 3-6 months, with fly ash railway infrastructure expected in coming months.
demand_pricing: Demand softer into April and May; management says it would be happy if the industry gets half of an intended price hike.
Industry prices rose about INR10/bag in March quarter (INR15-20 in select pockets); April over March trend cited at about INR10.
Premium gap versus base product: about INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium.
Pan-India peers' NSP reported close to each other; price gaps of INR5-10 by district.
Cost headwinds: freight up on higher lead distance and state additional goods tax (Himachal), packing costs disrupted in March by West Asia conflict, lower government incentives after GST rate cuts.

qa_highlights.question: Why is volume growth flat excluding Orient, and how is FY27 80 Mt achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management accepted Q4 volumes were muted and cited stabilization of Sanghi and Penna plus about 10 Mt of new capacity commissioning by September as the basis for FY27 growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the capacity reset a shift to inorganic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Primary focus remains organic; FY28 capacity target could slip one to two years, to FY30. Karan Adani said inorganic opportunities are evaluated but are not the priority.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 cost reduction net of current inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. INR4,500/t is the peak; INR250/t reduction from there gives about INR4,250/t average for FY27, with Q1 flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why is cost above the earlier INR4,000/t exit aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000/t was an aspiration for March exit, not a quarterly average; actual March was about INR4,100/t plus about INR250 war-related escalation. Drivers: branding, R&M, freight, packing, fuel and heat consumption, lower incentives.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capex reset and what is the IRR hurdle?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani cited project delays, wrong contractor choice, and projects started before engineering was complete; 6 months are being used for engineering. Project IRR hurdle is 18% on equity.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500/t cumulative cost cut a retreat from the INR3,650/t target?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not being abandoned; INR500/t is a committed minimum for two years, with more runway to the earlier target.

risks_watch: Cost trajectory: whether INR4,500/t peaks in Q4 and falls to about INR4,250/t average in FY27; Q1 FY27 expected flat.
Acquired asset utilization at Sanghi (57%) and Penna (46%) versus 65-70% and 55-60% targets.
Capex execution record and FY27 capex of INR6,000-6,500 crore against the earlier 155 Mt vision now pushed out.
Pricing power given soft demand and rising fuel and packing costs; April-May demand described as subdued.

Working capital: non-core working capital reportedly rose from about INR1,300 crore to INR5,500 crore; ACC negative operating cash flow tied to MSA receivables from Ambuja, expected to be settled via ICD.
Breakdowns and R&M overrun at Penna and Sanghi; higher branding spend (about INR70/t) to drive trade and premium sales.
summary.management_tone: Candid and defensive on execution: management acknowledged missed cost, capex and utilization targets and reset timelines, while repeatedly stressing controllable internal levers and confidence in the FY27 targets. Guidance on EBITDA per tonne was withheld as too uncertain given volatile energy costs.
key_quotes: Ambuja delivered a resilient performance for the year, achieving its highest ever annual sales volume of 73.7 million tonnes, up 16% Y-on-Y, year-on-year in that manner.
I strongly believe INR150 to INR200 savings will come from these components.
So we are not shying away from our target.
Yes, partially, there is a reset. We are not moving away from the target. Yes, we are moving away from the time line.

adds.what: About 10 Mt grinding/clinker capacity additions to be commissioned between now and September, taking capacity to ~119 Mt by end FY27
Proposed new clinker lines at Mundra (~2 Mt) and Assam limestone block (~2 Mt), targeted in ~24-28 months

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated volumes of ~80 Mt (~8% growth vs industry 5-5.5%), backed by ~10 Mt capacity commissioning by September and 119 Mt capacity by end FY27, though Q4 volumes were muted, acquired assets run at 46-57% utilisation, and FY27 capex was cut to INR6,000-6,500 crore with the FY28 capacity target pushed toward FY30.
